text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- FORD-Kenya faction leader Raila Odinga says his alliance with FORD-Asili's Kenneth Matiba is not based on fielding a single presidential candidate but on constitutional reforms as a prerequisite for the next general elections.
- Archbishop Raphael Ndingi Mwana a'Nzeki is installed as co-adjutor of the Roman Catholic Church Archdiocese of Nairobi.
- Five legislators of the ruling KANU party say the alleged split within the party is a creation of the opposition propagandists and the media.
- 22 cattle rustlers are killed in battle that leaves four homeguards dead in Samburu district of North Eastern Kenya.

- Islamic Party of Kenya leader Sheikh Khalid Balala, who says he was deprived of his Kenyan citizenship in 1994 while on a visit to Germany, writes to the Queen of England asking her to intervene in his plight to return to Kenya.
- Police arrest a man who allegedly obtained more than five million shillings from a Nairobi businessmen and civil servants while masquerading as a lawyer and businessman.

- The Roman Catholic Church primate of Nairobi, Cardinal Maurice Otunga, discloses that he is ready to retire from office and hand over duties to the newly appointed archbishop of Nairobi, Raphael Ndingi Mwana a'Nzeki.
- Former cabinet minister Paul Ngei is bailed out of his bankruptcy and immediately declares his return to active politics after a six-year political limbo.

- The hijacked Ethiopian airliner which crashed last Saturday killing more than 100 people had sought permission to refuel at Dar es Salaam International Airport but was turned away about an hour before it plunged into the Comoros Islands.
- Uganda's hopes for major debt relief are shattered at a Consultative Group aid meeting in Paris partly because the donors failed to agree on a consensus.
- Uganda promises to press for the suspension of the economic blockade on Burundi at the next summit meeting of regional leaders.
